body: Overall I like the look and feel of the Samsung health app. It seems to have some of the stuff I need. Fitbit shows calorie intake and calories burned and they calculate for you weather or not you have burned enough calories to stay in a certain range. To me that is a great incentive to be a little more active when I can see if I have burned enough calories to have a snack and still maintain a caloric deficit. And it isn’t just as simple as setting a calorie intake goal for the day. If I tell Fitbit I want to stay 200 intake calories below my calories burned it just adjusts throughout the day. If I have been more active it allows me to consume more. Also Fitbit has a very nice UPC (barcode) scanner option for when you are logging what you are eating. title: Poor cross platform support
body:
Some friends have Androids, some have iPhones. A bunch of them were already using Samsung Health, so we wanted to see if we could integrate and compete on steps during the week. Unfortunately iPhone users are not allowed to join step challenges with android users. Okay, fine.

But then we realized you can add friends to your leaderboard, regardless of platform, which is a huge win. Now though we can't do challenges together, we can use the leaderboard to informally compete over the 7 day rolling week. We are all fine with this.

Except we just realized for the iPhone folks, Samsung Health ONLY pulls steps from the iPhone itself as the data source, meaning that Apple Watch steps are not tracked at all. Despite the fact that I even disabled step tracking on the phone itself, and prioritized the Apple Watch in Apple Health as the #1 data source for step tracking, Samsung Health will not pull any steps at all unless they are from the iPhone. (None of us have Samsung watches)

This is a huge missed opportunity. If it's pulling data from Apple Health anyway, why can't it pull from different data sources? It's all in Apple Health already.

Once again, we are kind of back to square one on this.

title: Absolutely love my Gear Fit2 Pro & this app but have questions
body:
**UPDATED**
My husband bought me the watch a few years ago.  In over 30 years of marriage definitely one of his best choices!  At that time I used the Android app on my LG K20 VS501; despite what many have reported I never experienced any problems even while using Bluetooth headphones.
The Android app allowed me to access music from my phone directly from the app while using the exercise tab for tracking walking.  Additionally, I was able to receive distance, speed, pace etc. cues audibly which I could set through my settings.  That feature was a big help!
Fast forward:  last summer I moved into the iPhone XR.  I set everything up with the Apple apps.  Connects easily every time, & this app also allows for easy syncing.  At first I drove myself crazy trying to find my 2 favorite features:  the music icon & audible cues.  At first I thought the cues were just not coming through my headset but after trying it without headphones I discovered there were none, only countdown.  (Countdown also does not come through Bluetooth headset.). I even switched to the running tab, thinking the option would be there; nothing.  Yes, I tried without music:  no more nice fellow voice to encourage me.
Although the missing link to my music can be worked around I really miss the audible cues.  Am I missing something as to how to find such setup ( which was easy in Android)?  Is there a reason why those features are not in the app for Apple?
**Finally, one additional question:  although I have my step count set to be from my watch exclusively with the app (all shows correctly!) since my phone is not tied to my hip the integration with Apple’s Health app only shows my phone’s step count.  Why does the app’s step count not utilize my choice of source when combined with the health app?  I use the Health app to integrate with rewards for healthy living from Walgreens & AARP.
Thank you!

***Nice quick response***
It is a rare instance where a developer offers a response so quickly!  Thank You!
Just to clarify, I already have my step count source set to my Gear Fit2 Pro.  (For anyone working off reviews, the developer’s response is an excellent demonstration how to do such if you do not know how to select!)
My steps always record from my watch, syncing each time I open my SHealth app.  My daily goal is always in my view, one way or another.
I guess what I am asking is, although my watch step count is correct in the SHealth app, why does my Apple Health app only show my phone’s step count (as opposed to my selected step count source properly recorded)?  Yes, they are linked with SHealth being a data source allowing Apple Health to read.  I have tried entering the difference in steps manually but it never saves. 
Thank you, again! 
STAY SAFE EVERYONE & PLEASE keep Social Distancing!

title: Best health & activity tracking app
body:
I switched from Samsung galaxy s7 to iPhone X max (definitely will go back to Samsung again phone). This app is SO much better than apple’s health and activity apps and all other free of charge 3rd party apps in apple store. Why? All activity stats in 1 place and easily presented and working smoothly. Too bad Apple Watch doesn’t track sleep like Samsung watch gear sport (much better than I watch 3 in my opinion after using both).

Major pluses:
1) organization of the app and it’s free. The app includes sleep tracker, heart rate monitor, types of physical activities, etc. 
2) if u have Samsung watch, u score with this app. It works excellently with Samsung watch and transfers data. U can download Samsung watch app in apple store.
3) if u have no watch, u can select activity (running, walking or HIIT or barre) and turn it on to start tracking and then manually stop to get the stats. U won’t get heart rate measure unless u have watch or Samsung phone with the finger heart rate sensor. 
4) in case of Apple Watch, u can allow access for this app to get from apple’s health and activity apps (very annoying AND redundant that u have to look at both apps with terrible layout to see your data. 
5) app data presentation. I love how when u run/walk and click on the app and it shows u your route on the map, distance, time ran, calories burnt, heart rate and max heart rate (if u have watch and/or Samsung phone), steps and chart for all this. Then it tells u how it compares to your previous days (it’s duper nice how u see and switch between day and monthly activity) and to other people who use this app for your age, sex, fitness level, etc.

title: Much improved, but still buggy
body:

What I don't understand is why those take you to different interfaces for the same data. It's like the developers couldn't decide on an approach so they gave us both, but both are incomplete without the other view.

Syncing is much improved with the latest version of the software, plus a firmware update on my G3 watch. Biggest problem for me is a date/time bug which affects entering "dinner" details. Looks like it doesn't correctly account for your local timezone (I'm on EDT) so entries will disappear for today and show up instead for tomorrow. Sometimes it doesn't happen immediately, so you briefly see the totals you expect only to have them change. Super frustrating as it seems there's no good way for the user to correct it and force the date, and you can't delete the data for tomorrow until, well tomorrow. I've even seen it happen trying to correct data for the previous day despite having the date and time explicitly set.

Response to Developer:
I’m using the current version (1.5.0.035).
